rfi.title: How Cabo Delgado's riches became fuel for the Islamist insurgency in Mozambique
rfi.description: For almost a decade, an Islamist group has terrorised Mozambique's northern province of Cabo Delgado. Despite vast reserves of rubies, timber and natural gas, the region remains the country's poorest. This first instalment of Mozambique Exposed – an investigation coordinated by Forbidden Stories to which RFI contributed – examines how exploitation of the region's wealth, corruption and alleged abuses by security forces helped fuel the insurgency.

rfi.title: Children in danger 'not heard' in France, rights lawyer warns after Lyhanna death
rfi.description: The abduction and killing of 11-year-old French schoolgirl Lyhanna has catapaulted child protection to the top of France's political agenda – with President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday calling for full accountability and the government pledging full transparency. As investigators examine possible failures by the justice system, child rights lawyer Dominique Attias tells RFI professionals have been warning for years that vulnerable children are not being protected.

rfi.title: RFI denounces violation of press freedom after French reporter barred by Israel
rfi.description: RFI has condemned Israel's decision to refuse entry to journalist Alice Froussard, describing the move as "an obstacle to press freedom". Froussard, who reports on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict for French media, including RFI, was turned away on arrival at Tel Aviv airport and sent back without explanation.

rfi.description: Human-induced global warming is on track to reach 1.5C around 2030, a group of leading scientists said on Thursday.

rfi.title: Fifa grants World Cup accreditation to jailed French journalist Christophe Gleizes

rfi.title: French pop star Patrick Bruel charged with rape and sexual assault

rfi.title: Amnesty accuses Israel of ‘ethnic cleansing’ of West Bank Bedouin communities
rfi.description: Amnesty International has accused Israel of carrying out what it described as a state-led campaign of “ethnic cleansing” against Bedouin and herding communities in the occupied West Bank, saying the measures were intended to accelerate the annexation of Palestinian territory.

rfi.title: Europe faces growing threat from synthetic opioids and new drugs, report warns
rfi.description: Highly potent synthetic opioids are spreading through Europe's fast-changing drug market, linked to hundreds of deaths as traffickers shift to smaller ports and new smuggling methods, the European Union Drugs Agency (EUDA) has warned.

rfi.title: European heatwave drives world's second-hottest May on record

The pontiff arrived in Spain at the weekend for a week-long visit focused on immigration and politics.

lemonde.description: La revue « Science » publie, jeudi 11 juin, une cartographie planétaire de la densité des filaments mycorhiziens qui colonisent les racines de 70 % des espèces végétales terrestres, établissant avec elles des symbioses vitales. Un appel à préserver la bonne santé de ces réseaux fongiques.

Proteste in Israel: Ultraorthodoxe protestieren nach Festnahme von Wehrdienstverweigerern
zeit.description: In Israel protestieren ultraorthodoxe Juden gegen ihre Rekrutierung zur Armee. Wegen der Verweigerung hatte es mehrere Festnahmen gegeben. Es kam zu Ausschreitungen.

zeit.title: Irankrieg: Trump sagt Angriffe auf Iran wegen Gesprächen »auf höchster Ebene« ab

zeit.title: Heizungsgesetz: Linke prüft Klage gegen Heizungsgesetz nach Debatte im Bundestag
zeit.description: Die Kontroverse um das Heizungsgesetz geht weiter: Bei der ersten Lesung im Bundestag zeigt sich die Opposition unzufrieden. Die Linke erwägt sogar eine Klage.

zeit.title: »Disclosure Day« von Steven Spielberg: Die Siebziger wollen ihren Film zurück
zeit.description: In »Disclosure Day« lässt Steven Spielberg mal wieder Außerirdische aufmarschieren. Ein gelungenes Déjà-vu?

zeit.title: Siri AI: Warum die neue Siri nicht nach Europa kommt und wie vielleicht doch
zeit.description: Die gute Nachricht ist: Apples neue KI-Assistenz funktioniert tatsächlich. Die schlechte: nur in den USA. Dahinter steckt ein alter Streit. Aber es gibt Hoffnung.

observador.title: Montenegro diz que ainda há "caminho a percorrer" para PSU
observador.description: Em declarações aos jornalistas na Feira Nacional de Agricultura, Montenegro disse que a negociação em torno da PSU continua em curso, mas que o entendimento ainda não está fechado.

observador.title: A primeira cerimónia de abertura do Mundial 2026
observador.description:
O estádio Azteca, pela terceira vez palco de um Mundial, recebeu 99 mil pessoas. 
"Dai Dai" de Shakira e Burna Boy fechou a cerimónia de abertura, que contou com Salma Hayek e Andrea Bocelli.

observador.title: O que fazer no último fim de semana na Feira do Livro
observador.description: A 96.ª edição da Feira do Livro de Lisboa termina no domingo, 14 de junho, no Parque Eduardo VII. Entre debates e apresentações, os últimos três dias têm uma agenda preenchida. Fica aqui o essencial.

observador.title: Trump recua no Irão: estamos perto de um novo acordo de paz?
observador.description: João Albuquerque diz que o recuo de Donald Trump no Irão pode sinalizar uma abertura para um possível acordo. Acrescenta também que a Rússia intensificou os ataques após o apelo de Zelensky.

observador.title: Santarém recebe 450 milhões de euros para Mundial 2030
observador.description: O projeto "Viva Mundo" tem abertura prevista para 29 de abril de 2030 e é apresentado como uma infraestrutura "âncora com impacto económico e turístico à escala regional e nacional".

observador.title: Paltrow é cara de anúncio a prédio de luxo em Israel
observador.description: Atriz norte-americana promove o 51 Park, empreendimento residencial em Herzliya, em Israel. Está a ser criticada nas redes sociais por dar a cara pelo projeto israelita.

observador.title: Conferência Benfica. "Desculpas não nos levam a lado nenhum"
observador.description: Bruno Batista afirma que o Benfica carece de um projeto claro e deve focar no Seixal. Já Felipe Gomes sublinha que Marco Silva é o nome consensual para devolver o clube às vitórias.

observador.title: As notícias das 20h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Seguro defende alteração da Lei das Finanças Regionais
observador.description: No meio século de autonomia da Madeira, o chefe de Estado apelou à revisão da Lei das Finanças Regionais e defendeu que a gestão do mar da região deve sair de Lisboa.

observador.title: Fogo em Terras de Bouro combatido por 200 operacionais
observador.description: Sem casas ou bens em risco, o incêndio consome mato numa encosta de difícil acesso em Valdosende. Meios foram sendo reforçados desde as primeiras horas da manhã.

observador.title: Irão. Kallas alerta para "custo enorme" do regresso à guerra
observador.description: Depois de falar com os ministros iraniano e kuwaitiano, Kallas apelou à democracia e considerou os ataques do Irão "inaceitáveis": "um regresso a uma guerra em grande escala teria um custo enorme".

observador.title: Produção de petróleo na Rússia cai pelo 6º mês consecutivo
observador.description: A produção russa de petróleo recuou para cerca de 9 mil milhões de barris por dia. A contração deve-se, sobretudo, à intensificação dos ataques ucranianos contra infraestruturas energéticas russas.

observador.title: Ucrânia tenta estratégia para isolar a Crimeia?
observador.description: Um ataque ucraniano em larga escala atingiu pontes e infraestruturas na Crimeia ocupada. Há fontes que relatam que "Não restam pontes intactas nas vias de acesso terrestre à península".

observador.title: Lula e Sheinbaum criticam ingerência externa dos EUA
observador.description: Os líderes do Brasil e do México reuniram-se por videoconferência e alinharam posições depois de Washington ter desafiado os dois países com acusações e sanções.

observador.title: Chega/Açores. Parceria com EUA pode ser solução para porto
observador.description: Porto está classificado como infraestrutura estratégica no Acordo de Cooperação e Defesa entre Portugal e os EUA. Obras estimadas em 50 a 60 milhões de euros.

observador.title: Aguiar-Branco invoca Ferro Rodrigues na polémica do Chega
observador.description: PSD, Chega e CDS rejeitaram o recurso socialista. O presidente do Parlamento argumenta que o antecessor socialista agiu da mesma forma e que o PS nunca o questionou.

observador.title: "Não ficámos na mão de ninguém, controlámos sempre situação"
observador.description: Rui Costa fez balanço da temporada – mas falou sobretudo sobre o que se passou desde o final da época. Líder dos encarnados garante que Benfica aguenta um ano sem Champions e quer ganhar Liga Europa.

observador.title: Chega sem entendimento com Governo sobre reforma laboral
observador.description: André Ventura saiu de São Bento sem acordo com o primeiro-ministro. Descida da idade da reforma e reposição de dias de férias continuam a dividir os dois partidos.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026, les Ghetto Kids invités par Shakira à performer
france24fr.description: Les jeunes danseurs de la troupe des Ghetto Kids, composée d'enfants des rues d'Ouganda ont été invités à danser par Shakira lors de la mi-temps de la finale de la coupe du monde 2026. Une occasion en or pour ces jeunes âgés entre 4 et 16 ans de se faire connaître davantage, après être arrivés en finale du télécrochet « Britain's Got Talent »

france24fr.title: José Mourinho est officiellement de retour au Real Madrid jusqu'en juin 2029
france24fr.description: L'entraîneur portugais José Mourinho a été nommé jeudi sur le banc du Real Madrid pour les trois prochaines saisons, a annoncé le club madrilène. Il aura la lourde tâche de redresser la barre après une saison blanche pour les Merengue.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : la coupe de Trump ?
france24fr.description: Coup d’envoi ce jeudi de la Coupe du monde organisée conjointement par les États-Unis, le Mexique et le Canada. L’événement sportif le plus suivi de la planète s’ouvre dans un contexte géopolitique tendu. Avant même le premier coup de sifflet, Donald Trump est pointé du doigt pour sa politique autoritaire et les difficultés d’accès au territoire américain, où se déroulera la majorité des matchs.

france24fr.title: En direct : Trump annonce qu'il annule les frappes de jeudi contre l'Iran après des discussions "au plus haut niveau"
Trump dit "adorer" l’inflation, une "tentative désespérée de prouver qu’il contrôle la situation"
france24fr.description: Interrogé sur le taux de l’inflation aux États-Unis, qui a bondi de 4,2 % en un an, Donald Trump a salué mercredi des "chiffres supers", déclarant "adorer l’inflation", qu’il avait pourtant promis de faire "disparaitre" durant sa campagne.

france24fr.title: Mort de Lyhanna : un dysfonctionnement structurel de la justice ?
france24fr.description: La mort de Lyhanna a marqué une rupture de confiance des Français envers leurs institutions – notamment la justice, qui a échoué à protéger la jeune fille. Au-delà des responsabilités individuelles ou collectives, n’est-ce pas le système politique, en imposant ses lois ou ses visions successives, qui a éteint toute velléité pour les administrations de gagner en autonomie et de se corriger de l’intérieur ?

france24fr.title: Lutte contre les ingérences numériques : "La France est dans le top 3 européen"
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre Sébastien Lecornu a réuni jeudi les formations politiques pour aborder la question des ingérences électorales. À l’approche de la présidentielle, les autorités françaises redoutent des tentatives de manipulation numérique venues de l’étranger, dont l'efficacité est décuplée par les progrès de l'intelligence artificielle. Entretien avec Benoît Grünemwald, expert en cybersécurité à Eset.

france24fr.title: Le pape en Espagne : hommage aux migrants morts en mer
france24fr.description: En visite aux Canaries, le Pape Léon XIV a rendu hommage aux migrants morts dans l’Atlantique en lançant un bouquet de fleurs à la mer. Il a aussi dénoncé l’indifférence de beaucoup face à leur sort.

france24fr.title: Ambiance surchauffée au Mondial... Et ce n'est pas une bonne nouvelle!
france24fr.description:
Plusieurs matchs de ce Mondial vont se dérouler sous une chaleur écrasante. Des conditions qui pourront être difficiles à supporter pour les joueurs et pour les spectateurs. Toutes les équipes ne sont d'ailleurs pas logées à la même enseigne et cela peut influencer les résultats.
 
Comment la chaleur affecte la santé et les performance des footballeurs? On vous explique tout.

france24fr.title: Cette vidéo de la destruction d’un hélicoptère américain par l’Iran a été générée par IA
france24fr.description: Une supposée vidéo de la destruction d’un hélicoptère d’attaque américain Apache par l’armée iranienne a récolté plusieurs millions de vues sur les réseaux sociaux. Elle a pourtant été créée par intelligence artificielle.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : le Pentagone placé en confinement pour une fausse alerte
france24fr.description: Une partie du Pentagone, siège du département de la Défense américaine, a été placée jeudi en confinement et évacuée. Les pompiers sont intervenus pour un potentiel "incident lié à des matières ‌dangereuses", qui était en réalité une fausse alerte, selon CNN.

france24fr.title: Pour le 80e anniversaire de Donald Trump, la Maison Blanche prépare… une arène de MMA XXL
france24fr.description: Pour son anniversaire dimanche prochain, mais aussi pour les 250 ans de l’indépendance des États-Unis, Donald Trump et la Maison Blanche préparent un événement grandiose : une arène de MMA XXL où six combats d’UFC auront lieu.

france24fr.title: Ce qu'il faut dans sa valise quand on est un journaliste qui couvre la Coupe du monde
france24fr.description: Des objets utiles, nécessaires, voire absolument indispensables. Voici ce que contient la valise d'un journaliste qui part couvrir la Coupe du monde de football !

france24fr.title: RD Congo : des bénévoles de la Croix-Rouge attaqués en plein enterrement des victimes d'Ebola
france24fr.description: En RD Congo, la Croix-Rouge a dénonce, dans un communiqué, une attaque contre des volontaires lors d’une opération d’inhumation au cœur de l’épicentre de l’épidémie d’Ebola. Ces attaques sont de plus en plus fréquentes. Récit d'Emily Boyle.

france24fr.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Lecornu présente ses réponses face aux ingérences étrangères
france24fr.description: Désireux de "protéger le débat démocratique", Sébastien Lecornu expose jeudi aux partis politiques et à la presse les moyens pour mieux lutter contre les ingérences étrangères aux élections, qui pourraient s'intensifier à l'approche de la présidentielle.

france24fr.title: Royaume-Uni : démission du ministre britannique de la Défense, en désaccord avec Starmer
france24fr.description: Le ministre britannique de la Défense John Healey a annoncé jeudi sa démission, exprimant son désaccord avec le Premier ministre Keir Starmer à propos d'un plan d'investissement dans la défense qui doit être publié prochainement.

france24fr.title: Mondial-2026 : le Mexique, berceau ancestral du jeu de balle
france24fr.description: Le coup d’envoi de la Coupe du monde est donné à 21h, heure de Paris. Le Mexique ouvre la compétition. Malgré les manifestations, la fan zone du Zócalo à Mexico restera ouverte, assure la présidente Claudia Sheinbaum. C’est la troisième fois que le pays accueille le Mondial, un record lié à une longue tradition du jeu de balle dans la région, vieille de près de 3 500 ans.

france24fr.description: Le "futbol" s'apprête à reprendre ses droits avec le match d'ouverture du Mondial-2026 opposant le Mexique à l'Afrique du Sud jeudi à 13h00 locales, sur fond de tensions géopolitiques et de polémiques en séries.

spiegel.title: WM 2026 Live: Das Eröffnungsspiel Mexiko gegen Südafrika im Liveticker
spiegel.description: Der Ball rollt im Aztekenstadion, Gastgeber Mexiko traf bereits nach zehn Minuten gegen Südafrika. Dann kam die erste von 208 Trinkpausen des Turniers, seitdem klappt nicht mehr viel auf dem Rasen. Alles Wichtige zur WM.

spiegel.title: Spanische Liga: José Mourinho kehrt zu Real Madrid zurück
spiegel.description: Er soll Real Madrid wieder zu altem Glanz führen: Trainer José Mourinho kehrt nun auch offiziell zu dem Club zurück, den er vor mehr als einem Jahrzehnt bereits erfolgeich betreut hat.

spiegel.title: USA: Donald Trump nominiert Jay Clayton als neuen Geheimdienstkoordinator
spiegel.description: Mit seiner Interimslösung stieß er selbst bei Parteifreunden auf Kritik. Jetzt hat Donald Trump einen Kandidaten für die Nachfolge von Tulsi Gabbard als Geheimdienstkoordinator gefunden.

new-sci.title: Toy universe shows that time could be a quantum illusion
new-sci.description: An experiment with a toy universe made up of extremely cold atoms shows how time can emerge from quantum interactions, instead of existing by default

new-sci.title: Dramatic photo of ibis being guided to their winter homes wins award
new-sci.description: Student Gunnar Hartmann wins Nature’s 2026 Scientist at Work photography competition for this shot of migrating northern bald ibis in Spain

new-sci.title: The one film to watch before seeing Steven Spielberg’s Disclosure Day
new-sci.description: With Steven Spielberg’s new extraterrestrial film Disclosure Day just out, it’s the ideal time to watch Close Encounter of the Third Kind – perhaps the perfect UFO film, says film columnist Bethan Ackerley

new-sci.title: Ditching cigarettes for vapes may curb the cancer benefits of quitting
new-sci.description: A study of 4.5 million people suggests that ex-smokers who take up vaping are more at risk of dying from lung cancer than people who quit without the use of e-cigarettes

new-sci.title: New Scientist recommends a brilliant take on the evolution of birds
new-sci.description: Palaeontologist Steve Brusatte's The Story of Birds offers an excellent and sometimes startling account of bird evolution, finds Michael Marshall

new-sci.title: Think you have a good sense of humour? So do most people…
new-sci.description: Feedback is alarmed by a study that explored how funny people think they are, and discovered certain traits in those who rate themselves the most humorous

new-sci.title: Fully autonomous drones have killed human soldiers for the first time
new-sci.description: A senior figure in the Ukrainian defence industry told New Scientist that a test took place two years ago involving fully autonomous drones set to destroy anything in a given area, with confirmed casualties

new-sci.title: Wolves seen hunting European bison in rare camera-trap recording
new-sci.description: Europe’s largest land animal, the bison, is thought to be relatively unthreatened by predators, but footage from Białowieża Primaeval Forest in Poland shows it does face attacks from wolves

new-sci.title: Millions of fossil whale bones found in deep-ocean ‘necropolis’
new-sci.description: Researchers diving 7 kilometres deep in a crewed submersible have discovered a vast collection of whale bones, including fossils up to 5 million years old and species new to science

new-sci.title: Hundreds of new moons are revealing our solar system's violent history
new-sci.description: The outer solar system once seemed like a quiet backwater. But a glut of tiny, strange moons with unruly orbits are coming into view, revealing hints of a surprising past – and the origin of Saturn's rings

new-sci.title: A nuclear war between India and Pakistan could destroy the ozone layer
new-sci.description: Climate models suggest a small nuclear war in the tropics would do even more damage to the ozone layer than a larger nuclear war in more northerly latitudes, increasing exposure to dangerous ultraviolet radiation all over the world

new-sci.title: A Waymo nearly hit me, but I'm still optimistic about driverless cars
new-sci.description: A near miss with a Waymo while cycling through London hasn't changed my optimistic stance on driverless cars, but we can't ever let our guard down, says Matthew Sparkes

new-sci.title: Robots are about to overtake armed soldiers as the deciders of war
new-sci.description: Uncrewed ground vehicles have already been tested for defending the front line by the Ukrainian military. Despite their limitations, these remotely controlled robots could be the deciding factor in many conflicts

new-sci.title: Iron Age Britons may have removed the brains of the dead
new-sci.description: Scrape marks inside a skull and sharpened limb bones in a set of remains found in Scotland may be evidence of unusual Iron Age funerary rituals

new-sci.title: Frozen squirrel scat preserves ancient DNA from hundreds of species
new-sci.description: A complex ecosystem of woolly mammoths, bison, horses and big cats has been elucidated by studying the faeces of small rodents that probably ate the bigger animals

new-sci.title: The last-ditch plan to save coral reefs from utter destruction
new-sci.description: Bleaching has devastated reefs around the world, raising fears of an irreversible shift. Yet new interventions have revealed that corals can be remarkably resilient if we can give them enough help to recover

new-sci.title: Why we should all take quantum physics extremely personally
new-sci.description: Physics is considered a cold, hard science – but it will transform your life if you view it with a bit more subjectivity, says Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

new-sci.title: A cosmic case of mistaken identity that can only be solved right now
new-sci.description: Brown dwarfs are somewhere between the size of a planet and a star, so how could we have potentially mistaken two of them for distant galaxies? Columnist Chanda Prescod-Weinstein argues that solving this cosmic mix-up is particularly possible now, as galaxy research has never been stronger

phys-org.title: Open-source AI may aid climate and development but deepen inequality, experts warn
phys-org.description: Open-source artificial intelligence is advancing faster than the world can govern it, and the consequences could reshape the future of sustainability, democracy and global development. In a new comment published in Nature Communications, an international team of researchers warns that without coordinated action, open-source AI could also increase environmental pressures, deepen technological inequalities and facilitate the spread of misinformation.

phys-org.title: Salmonella genomes reveal 45 previously unknown toxins in foodborne bacteria
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of São Paulo (USP) in Brazil have discovered 45 new toxins produced by Salmonella bacteria, some of which are associated with foodborne infections. The study was conducted at the Center for Research in Bacterial and Bacteriophage Biology (B3 RIDC) and was published in the journal PLOS Biology. phys-org.title: Collapsing stars could spawn mini-universes, offering new path to gravastars
phys-org.description: Stars shine because atoms fuse in their interiors, releasing energy. When a very massive star has exhausted its nuclear fuel, radiation pressure can no longer provide sufficient counterforce to gravity. The star then collapses under its own mass until only a single point remains: the singularity.

phys-org.title: 'She should have seen it coming': How radicalization policies put the burden on Muslim mothers
phys-org.description: For several years now, the radicalization of young people has been making headlines. This phenomenon can be linked to the far-right movement, as we saw on May 30 in Shawinigan during a demonstration calling for a "White Québec," or revolve around other forms of radicalism, including Islamist movements.

phys-org.title: Sharks, seals, hunters, tourists: How wildlife‑human interactions matter for conservation
phys-org.description: Our relationships with wildlife are dynamic. They can change rapidly and unexpectedly.

phys-org.title: Chemists snap together complex 3D molecules from highly reactive 'radicals'—without losing their shape
phys-org.description: Building the complex 3D molecules needed for new medicines has always been a bit like assembling a puzzle with pieces that keep trying to flip over. Now, chemists at Scripps Research have found a way to snap two such molecular pieces together while keeping their original 3D shapes intact, even when using some of the most reactive molecules in chemistry: free radicals.

phys-org.title: Behind every overconfident leader might be a 'rational sycophant,' veteran game theorists find
phys-org.description: The past and present are rife with examples of advisers convincing leaders of the benefits of launching an ill-advised war, or downplaying the risks of a potentially fatal flaw in the design of a car or spacecraft.

phys-org.title: Cyclone Gabrielle-style storms may unleash tens of thousands more North Island landslides
phys-org.description: In 2023, Cyclone Gabrielle triggered an estimated 800,000 landslides across the North Island, making it one of the most extreme landslide events ever recorded. New research by Te Whare Wānanga o Waitaha | University of Canterbury (UC) and Earth Sciences New Zealand suggests that under a warmer climate, future storms similar to Cyclone Gabrielle could be even more extreme, triggering tens of thousands more landslides across parts of the North Island and highlighting the need for targeted planning

phys-org.title: Carbon dioxide removal slow to take off, alarming scientists
phys-org.description: Carbon dioxide removal experts have sounded the alarm in Milan this week over a shortfall in research and investment in the nascent sector viewed as essential for mitigating climate change.

phys-org.title: Smuggled dinosaur fossils return to Mongolia after two decades
phys-org.description: Mongolia has recovered a rare dinosaur skeleton and a trove of fossils illegally exported two decades ago, authorities said Wednesday, concluding years of efforts to return the paleontological treasures.

phys-org.title: This is how supermassive black holes feed themselves
phys-org.description: How supermassive black holes (SMBHs) in the centers of galaxies accrete material, how they feed back into the surrounding region, and how they regulate these processes to influence the evolution of their galaxies are all hot topics in astronomical and astrophysical research. Astronomers are nearly certain that all large galaxies like the Milky Way have an SMBH, and detailed observations of them are where answers will be found. But only some galaxies are readily observed in detail, even by the po

phys-org.title: Forest gaps and deadwood boost bird and bat diversity in woodlands
phys-org.description: Disorder brings more life to the forest: Birds and bats react to this in different ways. This is shown by a new study from the University of Würzburg's Biocenter.

phys-org.title: Indoor urban agriculture isn't necessarily low carbon, study shows
phys-org.description: Growing lettuce indoors in Canadian cities can be as climate-friendly as conventional farming, but only in regions where electricity comes from renewable sources and is therefore low-carbon, according to a new McGill-led study.

phys-org.title: First global map of mycorrhizal fungi reveals true scale of underground networks across the planet
phys-org.description: Mycorrhizal fungi form underground networks that sustain plant life and help regulate Earth's climate by drawing carbon into soils. In a study published in Science, an international team of researchers produced the first global maps estimating the distribution and mass of the Earth's arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal networks.

phys-org.title: Organic molecule with ultranarrow emission spectrum could lead to better LEDs
phys-org.description: Over the past several decades, light sources have gradually transitioned to light-emitting diodes, or LEDs, and inorganic LEDs are now used across a wide range of applications. In parallel, organic LEDs, or OLEDs, have become widely used in display technologies.

phys-org.title: Physicists introduce phase contrast to electron microscopy, delivering sharper images of our body's tiniest proteins
phys-org.description: Nearly 100 years ago, a seemingly simple discovery revolutionized the microscope. The introduction of phase contrast, which garnered a Nobel Prize in 1953, brought into clear view structures inside cells that had previously been too faint or washed out for biologists to study.

phys-org.title: Prescribed fires can cut smoke pollution for years, miles beyond burn areas
phys-org.description: A new study finds that burning 500,000 acres (202,000 hectares) of California conifer forests each year with prescribed fire could cut deadly pollution from wildfire smoke by roughly 10% over a decade.

phys-org.title: Overlooked pollutants are responsible for about 15% of current global warming, study shows
phys-org.description: In a new paper published in Science, leading scientists and climate policy experts show that 15% of current global warming (0.3°C) from human emissions stems from pollutants that fall outside most existing climate policy frameworks. Most of these overlooked pollutants are called "indirect greenhouse gases" and include carbon monoxide, non-methane volatile organic compounds, nitrogen oxides and molecular hydrogen.

arxiv-ai.description:

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.11337v1 Announce Type: new

arxiv-ai.description:

arxiv-ai.description:

arxiv-ai.description:

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.11522v1 Announce Type: new

arxiv-ai.description:

arxiv-ai.description:
arXiv:2606.11634v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The rapid progress of reasoning and agentic large language models (LLMs) has increased the demand for long-context inference, but self-attention (SA) scales quadratically with context length.

arxiv-ai.description:

Abstract: Touch is a key modality for embodied agents to understand the physical world. arxiv-ai.description:

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

A euphemism for culled fetal lambs? Or perhaps a medieval misapprehension of cotton? Thom Sliwowski traces the roots of this fabled zoophyte.

proj-syn.title: The Democrats Need a Story, Not More Lists
proj-syn.description: Whereas Donald Trump has offered voters a clear and compelling narrative, Democrats have provided only vague aspirations and long lists of policies. To win over voters—rather than scrounging protest votes—they must articulate a compelling economic vision, with wage-led growth as its foundation.

proj-syn.title: What if Europe Loses Access to Its Climate Data?
proj-syn.description: The European Green Deal runs on data, from corporate disclosures to climate-risk analyses and decarbonization pathways. But much of this data feeds platforms and tools developed outside the European Union, which could threaten the bloc’s climate agenda and even its foundational values.

proj-syn.title: Raising Interest Rates Won’t Stabilize African Inflation
proj-syn.description: Monetary tightening in Africa would not only fail to rein in inflation; it would raise the cost of productive investment, suppress growth, and hamper the continent's much-needed structural transformation. A better strategy would focus on accelerating this transformation by channeling finance into productive industries.

proj-syn.title: Peak Oil Demand Has Arrived
proj-syn.description: Amid the disruptions caused by the US/Israeli-Iran war, countries have begun adapting to life with less oil. What started as a supply shock has become a demand story, forcing the energy sector to reconsider one of its most important assumptions: continued growth of global oil demand.

proj-syn.title: The Enduring Enigma of Economic Growth
proj-syn.description: Developing countries have made enormous progress in many of the factors behind growth, reflected in stronger institutions, rising education levels, higher life expectancy, and increased investment rates. Yet income convergence with advanced economies has been painfully slow—and in most cases absent.

proj-syn.title: Is the US Stock Market Too Big?
proj-syn.description: With China and India having grown so fast as to compensate for the underperformance of their fellow BRICS (Brazil, Russia, and South Africa), the center of gravity in the global economy continues to shift eastward. The question now is whether—and when—equity valuations will reflect this underlying reality.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Bad Vibes
proj-syn.description: A government that abandons structural agendas whenever sentiment turns negative will still be managing sentiment four years later—with nothing to show for it. Brazil’s “vibecession” is a real problem for the current government; but winning the news cycle is not a real solution.

proj-syn.title: Negotiating With the Antichrist
proj-syn.description: Apocalyptic thinking is seeping into the political discourse, with figures like Peter Thiel, Pete Hegseth, and Aleksandr Dugin portraying political differences as struggles between good and evil. When rivals become mortal enemies, the instruments of politics and diplomacy cannot work.

proj-syn.title: Why Is Europe’s Economy Falling Short?
proj-syn.description: For much of the postwar era, European policymakers have prioritized stability and predictability over fostering breakthrough innovation. Today, as the United States and China compete for AI dominance, a stagnant Europe is struggling to regain its place at the technological frontier.

proj-syn.title: Big Tech’s Shadow Market Power
proj-syn.description: Big Tech firms are amassing market power through strategies that bypass current rules for oversight, investigation, and intervention. Unless and until regulators account for the full scope and scale of these strategies, Silicon Valley’s dominance will remain unchallenged.

proj-syn.title: The AI Revolution Mirrors the Green Transition
proj-syn.description: The need for massive upfront investments and the likelihood of significant job displacement imply remarkable parallels between the AI buildout and the green transition. In both cases, the state has an important role to play in guiding market forces on behalf of the public good.

proj-syn.title: Where Is China’s Trillion-Dollar Trade Surplus Going?
proj-syn.description: Whereas China’s trade surplus used to be absorbed largely by the central bank and channeled into official reserves, it is now being redeployed by private actors in search of yield. This indicates China’s progress on financial deepening and underscores markets' increasingly central role in shaping the economy.

proj-syn.title: The Future of Development Finance Is Not Primarily About Money
proj-syn.description: Multilateral development banks have not kept pace with changes to the global financial environment. For middle-income countries like India, accessing knowledge and technology is now a bigger challenge than raising capital, which suggests that these institutions must rethink their operating model.

proj-syn.title: Nigeria’s Perilous French Gambit
proj-syn.description: Nigeria’s increasingly close relationship with France marks a departure from six decades of foreign policy aimed at reducing French influence in West Africa. An increasingly close relationship with a power that has long sought to undermine Nigerian influence in West Africa will benefit only politically connected business elites.

proj-syn.title: Autocracy Is Fueling Mexico’s Fiscal Deterioration
proj-syn.description: Mexico’s recent ratings downgrades are merely a symptom of a more serious malady: the ruling Morena party’s efforts to consolidate power permanently. To ensure the legal predictability foreign investors require, President Claudia Sheinbaum would need to confront Morena’s ideological legacy and, more importantly, its cartel ties.

proj-syn.title: The Trump Economy Is Bad News for Republicans
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump triumphed in the 2024 election by continually hammering on the Biden administration’s dismal inflation record. If his party gets shellacked in this year’s midterm elections, it will be because he has made Americans even worse off.

proj-syn.title: SpaceX Is the New East India Company
proj-syn.description: Although SpaceX is not about to rule over foreign subjects, as the chartered companies founded in the early modern era did, it, too, is operating beyond the reach of any sovereign. And like its predecessors, it has already accumulated immense powers that governments will struggle to reclaim.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Should Not Raise Interest Rates Yet
proj-syn.description: Against a backdrop of acute uncertainty, weak growth, subdued wages, and elevated market interest rates, monetary tightening is warranted only when there is convincing evidence that higher inflation is becoming entrenched. No such evidence has yet materialized in Europe.
